newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Biochim Bank has 66 bln lvs profit in '96.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Biochim Bank has 66 bln lvs profit in '96.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-owned Biochim Bank posted a pre-tax profit of 66 billion levs for 1996, which would be fully set aside as provisions, the bank's executive director said on Thursday.
"The pre-tax profit for last year will be fully set aside as provisions against bank's risk assets," Vladimir Georgiev told Reuters after an extraordinary shareholders' meeting.

Under local accountancy standards, due to be brought in line with international requirements from this year commercial banks set aside provisions from their pre-tax profit instead of entering them as expenditures in their balance sheets.

Biochim Bank had a capital-to-risk assets ratio of five percent at the end of last year after it managed to collect some risk loans and received long-term government securities worth $81 million to boost its capital.
"Last year the bank managed to collect risk loans worth 7.5 billion levs and over $110 million, which made some 25 percent of its credit portfolio denominated in foreign currency," Georgiev said.
The shareholders also decided to appoint Gancho Kolev as a member of bank's supervisory board after Dimitar Nenkov tendered his resignation.
Kolev, whose term of office as deputy governor of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) expired in June, has been an advisor of the BNB governor Liubomir Filipov since then.
Biochim Bank was set up through a merger of former Biochimbank, Sofia Bank and Serdika Bank in August 1995 by the Bank Consolidation Company (BCC).
The BCC, which manages state equity into local commercial banks, holds over 98 percent of Biochim Bank's share capital. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
